title.narrative: IQ: Basra Electricity Dissemination and Development Project (EDDP)

description.narrative: The development objective of Electricity Services Reconstruction and Enhancement Project for Iraq is to improve the reliability and operational and commercial efficiency of electricity services in the selected project areas. This project contains three components. 1) The first component, South Electricity Transmission Network Reinforcement, supports a range of activities designed to: (i) address network capacity limitations to meet existing electricity power demand, (ii) meet expected future load growth, (iii) provide operation flexibility and hence improved electricity supply reliability, and (iv) reduce transmission network technical losses. 2) The second component, South Electricity Distribution Network Reconstruction and Reinforcement and SEDC Electricity Sales Revenue Management Improvement, support activities related to: (i) distribution network rehabilitation and reinforcement to meet current and future electricity demand, reduce technical losses, and increase operations flexibility, including distribution substations and lines; and (b) the design, supply, installation, and commission of an IDMIS covering electricity distribution core business functions namely network planning, operations and maintenance, commercial, and management of corporate resources. 3) The third component, Institutional Capacity Strengthening and Project Implementation Support, aims to include institutional capacity building aligned with the government reform program for improved accountability, governance, financial sustainability, and increased private sector participation.
To improve the reliability and operational efficiency of electricity services in the selected project areas.

condition.narrative: SETC and SEDC shall each maintain, throughout Project implementation, Project Management Teams with an institutional framework,functions, and resources, including competent personnel in adequate numbers, satisfactory to the Bank for such purpose.

SETC and SEDC shall establish a Project Coordinating Committee, not later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, andmaintain at all times during Project implementation, said Committee, comprising representatives of SETC and SEDC and with aninstitutional framework, functions, and resources satisfactory to the Bank for such purpose.

The Project Implementing Entity shall appoint, not later than six (6) months after the Effective Date, and thereafter maintainthroughout Project implementation, an Owner's Engineer with qualifications, experience, and terms of reference satisfactory to theBank.

Women reported engaging in income-generating activities (IGA) due to improvements in electricity service

comment.narrative: Women reported engaging in income-generating activities due to improvements in electricity service (number). Project target was identified based on information from Iraq's Central Bureau of Statistics, which has sex-disaggregated, region-specific data points from the LFS survey (2008). The share of economically active women is on average 9 percent in the project areas compared to the national average of 18 percent. The project aims to close this regional gap and identified 20 percent as the target. According to Feb 2024 survey (conducted by CLIC - SEDC consultants), the target of 20% has been achieved.

title.narrative: Customers satisfied with service provided by SEDC

comment.narrative: In February 2024, the Baseline Report Basra Electricity Services Reconstruction and Enhancement Project (BEDDP) was finalized by the consultant (CLIC) in coordination with SEDC and the World Bank task team. The survey reports that the baseline value of the percentage of customers who are satisfied with SEDC's services is 65 percent. The survey measured customer satisfaction across the 6 dimensions of: (1) using electricity to carry out daily household tasks; (2) using electricity to carry out school/college related tasks; (3) using electricity to carry out business-related/job related tasks; (4) level of safety when using electricity; (5)reliability of the electricity network and (6) voltage consistency. Once the network improvements are completed, SEDC will conduct a follow up survey across these 6 dimensions to assess whether and to what degree there is an increase in the percentage of customers satisfied with its services.

Women-owned businesses reporting increased income due to improved electricity services (percentage)

comment.narrative: Women-owned businesses reporting increased income due to improved electricity services (percentage). Project target was identified based on information from the Enterprise Survey in Iraq (2011). Access to electricity is the foremost obstacle among businesses, especially when disaggregating by gender of top managers. According to Feb 2024 survey, most of the women business owners (73%) reported daily losses due to electricity supply services issues. Therefore, the baseline and target values for this indicator remain the same at 0% and 20%, respectively
